FOREWORD 


This Indian Standards was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards after the draft finalized by the Footwear 
Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Division Council. 


Municipal workers are exposed to unhygienic conditions during their work. They can come in contact with 
infectious contaminants, dangerous substances such as glass shard, needles etc., and often have to work in 
water-logged areas. 


Footwear framed under this specification has the limited scope for use in scavenging work and waste handling 
in dry and wet condition for day to day use. Occupational footwear is to be used for light work and protective 
footwear is to be used for conditions where foot protection is important. Non-leather shoes are specified here since 
municipal workers have to work in wet conditions, for which leather is not suitable. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with the final 
value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS 2 : 1960 ‘Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)’. The number of significant places retained in the 
rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 16994 : 2018 


Indian Standard 


FOOTWEAR FOR MEN AND WOMEN FOR 
MUNICIPAL SCAVENGING WORK 


1 SCOPE 


This standard prescribes requirements and method 
of sampling and test for protective and occupational 
footwear for use in municipal scavenging work. 


2 REFERENCES 


The standards listed in Annex A contain provisions 
which, through reference in this text, constitute 
provisions of this standard. At the time of publication, 
the editions indicated were valid. All standards are 
subject to revision, and parties to agreements based 
on this standard are encouraged to investigate the 
possibility of applying the most recent editions of the 
standards, listed in Annex A. 


3 TERMINOLOGY 


3.1 Classifications 


Footwear made of material other than leather, can 
belong to class (I) vide 4 of IS 15298 (Part 3) and 
IS 15298 (Part 4). 


All polymer/elastomer/rubber footwear belong to class 
(II) vide 4 of IS 15298 (Part 3) and IS 15298 (Part 4). 


3.2 Polymer 


Polymeric materials are as per definition in 3.4 of 
IS 15298 (Part 3) and IS 15298 (Part 4) and as defined 
under harmonized system of nomenclature (HSN) as 
good to fall under chapter head of 39. 


3.3 Rubber 


Rubber materials are as per definition in 3.3 of 
IS 15298 (Part 3) and IS 15298 (Part 4) and as defined 
under harmonized system of nomenclature (HSN) 
as goods to fall under chapter head of 40. 


3.4 Elastomer 


All types of blended polymer (TPO, TPR), grafted 
polymer, co-polymer etc. which exhibits rubber like 
property and thermo form/set and used for production 
of footwear. 


3.5 Protective Footwear for Professional use 


Footwear incorporating protective features to protect 
the wearer from injuries which could arise through 
accidents in the working area and the footwear is 
designed to give protection against impact when tested 
at a minimum energy level of 100 J and compression at 
a load of minimum 10 KN. 


3.6 Occupational Footwear for Professional use 


Footwear incorporating features suitable for operation 
in general condition (wet condition of minimal impact) 
and in rain, in day to day use in related working areas 
so as to protect the feet. 


3.7 Protective Toe Cap 


Component of footwear designed to protect the toes 
of the wearer from impacts up to an energy level of 
minimum 100 J and compression load of minimum 
10 kN. 


3.8 Compact Outsole/Heel 


Suitable polymer/rubber/elastomer having density not 
less than 0.9 g/cm’. 


3.9 Compact Insole and Insocks 


Suitable rubber/polymer/elastomer having density not 
less than 0.9 g/cm? coated with textile. 


3.10 Lining 
Material covering the inner surface of the upper. 


Vamp lining is material covering the inner surface of 
the forepart of the upper. 


Quarter lining is material covering the inner surface of 
the quarter of the upper. 


3.11 Non-Leather Upper 


Upper made out of coated/laminated textile matter 
(synthetic leather or equivalent); or textile at face and 
lined with textile; or split leather; or suitable textile 
material and to meet the requirement vide clause 5.4.2, 
5.4.3, 5.4.4, 5.4.5, 5.4.8 of IS 15298 (Part 3) and 
IS 15298 (Part 4) and to fall under Class I of 
IS 15298 (Part 3) and IS 15298 (Part 4). 


3.12 Polymeric/Elastomeric Upper 


Upper made out of suitable polymer/elastomer at 
face and having textile at the back and leak proof; the 
footwear may belong to class I of IS 15298 (Part 3) and 
IS 15298 (Part 4) or class II of IS 15298 (Part 3) and 
IS 15298 (Part 4). 


3.13 Rubber Upper 


Upper made out of rubber and having textile at the back 
and leak proof; the footwear may belong to class I of 
IS 15298 (Part 3) and IS 15298 (Part 4) or class II of 
IS 15298 (Part 3) and IS 15298 (Part 4). 


IS 16994 : 2018 


3.14 Bi Polymer/Bi Density Outsole 

Outsoles made out of two or more polymer/elastomer/ 
rubber and having different density. Performance 
requirements shall comply with clause 5.8.6 of 
IS 15298 (Part 3) and IS 15298 (Part 4). 

3.15 Insocks 

Polymeric material with textile lining having design to 
support the bottom of the feet for comfort. 

3.16 Toe Spring of Footwear 


The vertical distance between the bottom of the 
footwear at the extreme toe and the ground plane in its 
normal orientation. 


4 TYPES AND VARIETIES 


4.1 Municipal scavenging footwear can be of one of the 
following types: 


a) Type 1 — Shoes 


b) Type 2 — Ankle Boots 
c) Type 3 — Wellington / Gum Boots 


4.2 The condition of work can vary as given below: 
a) Variety 1 — For use in dry condition 
b) Variety 2 — For use in wet and slurry condition 


c) Variety 3 — For use in waterlogged and other 
slurry conditions where ankle height shoes are 
incapable to protect. 


5 DESIGN 


Common designs for shoes and boots are given below 
but these designs are not mandatory. Design shall be as 
agreed to between the purchaser and the manufacturer. 


6 FITTINGS 


Fittings of the footwear will be in conformity to Table 9 
for men and Table 8 for women of IS 1638 and suitably 
matching to manufacturer’s last. 


Type 1 
Class I or II [IS 15298 (Part 3) and (Part 4)] 


Type 2 
Class — II [IS 15298 (Part 3) and (Part 4)] 


Type 3 
Class — II [IS 15298 (Part 3) and (Part 4)] 


Fic. 1 TYPES OF MUNICIPAL SCAVENGING FOOTWEAR 


7 MATERIALS AND PROPERTIES 
7.1 Protective Toe Cap 


Protective toe cap is to be provided in manufacturing 
of protective footwear for variety 2 and 3 of work and 
shall meet the prescribed requirement of impact test 
and compression test as prescribed in clauses 5.3.2.3 
and 5.3.2.4 in IS 15298 (Part 3). 


7.2 Use of Polymer/Elastomer/Rubber 


Mono or bi density or bi polymer or polymer with 
rubber insert at bottom will be used as per selection and 
as agreed to between the manufacturer and purchaser or 
as per sample (approved). 


For Varieties 2 and 3 work suitable polymer/elastomer/ 
rubber is to be used as agreed by manufacturer and 
consumers. 


7.3 Upper 


7.3.1 Footwear falling in Class I should satisfy 
requirements given in clauses 5.4.3 and 5.4.6 of 
IS 15298 (Part 3) when tested in accordance with 
clauses 6.3, 6.6 and 6.8 of IS 15298 (Part 1). 
Footwear falling in Class II should satisfy 
requirements given in clauses 5.4.2, 5.4.4, 5.4.6 
and 5.4.8 of IS 15298 (Part 3) and IS 15298 (Part 4) 
when tested in accordance with clauses 6.1, 6.4, 6.6, 
6.8 and 6.10 of IS 15298 (Part 1). 


7.3.2 Flexing requirement of upper for Class II 
footwear when tested in accordance with clause 6.5 
of IS 15298 (Part 1) and should meet the requirement 
prescribed in clause 5.4.5 of IS 15298 (Part 3) and 
IS 15298 (Part 4). 


7.4 Lining 


Lining for quarter and vamp for footwear belonging 
to class I, when tested in accordance with clauses 6.3, 
6.6, 6.8 and 6.12 of IS 15298 (Part 1) shall meet the 
respective prescribed requirements in clauses 5.5.1, 
5.5.2 and 5.5.3 in IS 15298 (Part 3) and IS 15298 
(Part 4). 


For footwear falling under class II, the lining for 
quarter and vamp shall meet the prescribed requirement 
in clause 5.5.2 in IS 15298 (Part 3) and (Part 4) 
when tested in accordance with clause 6.12 in 
IS 15298 (Part 1). 


7.5 Insoles/Insocks 


Insole/insocks shall meet the requirements of clauses 
5.7.1, 5.7.3 and 5.7.4 in IS 15298 (Part 3) and (Part 4) 
when tested in accordance with clauses 7.1, 7.2, 7.3 and 
6.12 of IS 15298 (Part 1). 


7.6 Counter Stiffener 


Counter stiffener shall be provided wherever is 
applicable and shall meet specification of IS 7554. 


IS 16994 : 2018 


7.7 Outsole Heel 


Material to be used as outsole heel shall have density 
not less than 0.9 g/cm? and compact. 


Thickness of Out Sole Hardness of Outsole 
and Heel 
i) Fore With Cleat: Hardness (IRHD): 60 + 5 
part 10mm(min) Change in hardness 
Without Cleat: after accelerated ageing 
6 mm (min) when rubber is used, is 
ii) Heel WithCleat: + 5/—2 at 1004 2°C for 
15 mm (min) 24 h when tested as per 
; IS 3400 (Part 4). 
Without Cleat: 
9 mm (min) 


7.7.1 Tear Strength of Outsole 


When outsole is tested in accordance with clause 8.2 of 
IS 15298 (Part 1), type 3 footwear shall satisfy a tear 
strength of at least 8 kN/m. 


When outsole tested in accordance with clause 8.2 of 
IS 15298 (Part 1), footwear of type | and type 2 shall 
satisfy tear strength of at least 8 kN/m for a material 
having density higher than 0.9 g/cm? and 5 kN/m for 
material having density equal to 0.9 g/cm’. 


7.7.2 Abrasion Resistance of Outsole/Heel 


When outsole/heel of Type 1 footwear belonging 
to Class I, is tested in accordance with clause 8.3 of 
IS 15298 (Part 1), the relative volume loss shall not be 
more than 250 mm? for materials with density equal 
to 0.9 g/cm*; and the volume loss shall not be more 
than 150 mm? for materials with density more than 
0.9 g/cm’. 

When outsole/heel of Type I footwear belonging to 
Class II, and Type 2 and Type 3 footwear is tested 
in accordance with clause 8.3 of IS 15298 (Part 1), 


the relative volume loss shall not be more than 
250 mm. 


7.7.3 Flexing Resistance of Outsole/Heel 


When outsole/heel is tested in accordance with clause 
8.4 of IS 15298 (Part 1), the cut growth shall not be 
greater than 4 mm before 30000 flex cycles. 


7.7.4 Interlayer Bond Strength 


When outsole/heel is tested in accordance with clause 
5.2 of IS 15298 (Part 1) the bond strength between 
the layer shall not be less than 4.0 N/mm unless there 
is tear at any point of outsole and in such case, bond 
strength shall not be less than 3.0 N/mm. 


7.7.5 Upper-outsole Bond Strength 


When tested in accordance with clause 5.2 of 
IS 15298 (Part 1) the bond strength shall not be less than 


IS 16994 : 2018 


4.0 N/mm, unless there is tearing of the sole and in 
such case the bond strength shall not be less than 
3.0 N/mm. 


7.8 Insocks 


Polymeric/rubber/elastomer material with lining. 


7.9 Hydrolysis 


When bottom sole or other components are made out 
of polyurethane the same shall be tested in accordance 
with clause 8.5 of IS 15298 (Part 1) and the same shall 
comply with clause 5.8.5 of IS 15298 (Part 3) and 
IS 15298 (Part 4). 


7.10 Ageing Test of Whole Footwear 


When rubber is used for manufacture of footwear 
the whole footwear shall be subjected to ageing test at 
100 + 1°C for 24 h and shall not develop any tackiness 
or brittleness. 


8 CONSTRUCTION 


Footwear falling under class I or II can be manufactured 
in any process as suitable. The footwear shall not 
have any banned chemicals listed in Annex B of the 
specification. 


When PVC is used as polymer, virgin PVC compound 
shall only be used. 


Footwear so manufactured shall have minimum toe 
spring of 15 mm. 


Whenever protective footwear is manufactured the 
same shall have protective toe cap and shall meet 
the impact resistance and compression resistance as 
prescribed in this specification. 


Type | footwear is to be provided with lace or velcro 
fastening or as agreed to between the manufacturers and 
the purchasers and as per design. Minimum breaking 
load of lace shall be 600 N when tested between 
18 cm grip length in accordance with the method given 
in Annex C. 


Type 2 footwear shall have suitable fastening 
arrangement as per design, with either velcro fastening 
device or press button. 


Insocks of suitable material shall be provided for 
Type 1 and 2 footwear. Purchaser may indent insocks, 
which shall be optional for Type 3. 


8.1 Height of Upper 


Footwear of type | shall conform to Design A as given 
in Fig 3 in IS 15298 (Part 3) and IS 15298 (Part 4). 


Footwear of type 2 shall conform to Design B as given 
in Fig 3 in IS 15298 (Part 3) and IS 15298 (Part 4). 


Footwear of type 3 shall conform to Design C or D 
as given in Fig 3 in IS 15298 (Part 3) and IS 15298 
(Part 4). 


8.2 Internal Length of Toe Cap 


Whenever protective footwear is manufactured, 
same shall have protective toe cap; internal length of 
the protective toe cap shall meet the requirement as 
prescribed in clause 5.3.2.2 and table 5 of IS 15298 
(Part 3) when tested in accordance with clause 5.3 of 
IS 15298 (Part 1). 


8.3 Impact Resistance and Compression Resistance 
of Protective Footwear 


Protective footwear shall meet the requirements of 
impact resistance and compression resistance as 
prescribed in clause 5.3.2.3 vide table 6 and 5.3.2.4 of 
IS 15298 (Part 3). 


8.4 Volatility and Lead (Pb) Content when PVC is 
the Polymer 


When tested in accordance with IS 12240 (Part 4) the 
volatile content shall not be more than 2 percent by 
mass. 


When tested in accordance with IS 12240 (Part 5) the 
lead content shall not be more than 2 ppm. 


8.5 Restriction of Colour when PVC is Used as 
Polymer 


No footwear having polymer of PVC shall be made in 
black colour. 


NOTE — This is required to stop use of scrap of PVC including 
medical waste as much as possible which is practiced in 
abundant and is a hazard. 


8.6 Leak Proof Test of Whole Footwear for Variety 
2 and 3 Work 


When footwear for Variety 2 and 3 work is tested 
in accordance with 5.7 of IS 15298 (Part 1), it shall 
comply with 5.3.3 of IS 15298 (Part 3) 


9 FINISH OF FOOTWEAR 


In appearance, general workmanship and in all other 
respect with regard to looks of boots, they shall be 
matching the approved sample of the purchaser. 


Packing of the finished goods will be as agreed between 
the purchaser and manufacturer. 


10 MARKING 


10.1 Each boot shall be permanently marked with the 
following: 


a) Size, 
b) Manufacturer’s name/brand, 
c) Year and month of manufacture, 


d) Number and year of the standard, based upon 
which boots are produced, that is, protective or 
occupational boot, and 


e) Any other statutory marking. 


10.2 BIS Certification Marking 


The shoes may also be marked with the Standard Mark. 
All markings shall be at the side of tongue or at top 
outer face of the boot so that least damage is done 
during working. 


10.2.1 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by 
the provisions of Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 
and the Rules and Regulations made there under. The 
details of the conditions under which the licence for use 
of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers 
or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of 
Indian Standards. 


11 INFORMATION TO BE SUPPLIED 


Each pair of boot shall be supplied with information in 
English and Hindi as follows: 

a) Name and full address of manufacturer, 

b) Detail of customer care service provider, 


IS 16994 : 2018 


c) Instruction for storage and maintenance, 


d) Drying procedure of wet boots and cleaning of 
boots for proper service, 


e) Obsolescence dead line or period of obsolescence, 


f) Wherever applicable declaration to be made 
stating footwear is not for application at specific 
areas with statutory warning etc. for electrical 
resistance and other specific special purposes 
etc.

stating footwear is not for use in fire hazard/ 
explosion prone areas and in hot contact areas, 
and

ANNEX C 
( Clause 8 ) 


METHOD FOR DETERMINATION OF BREAKING LOAD AND 
ELONGATION AT BREAK FOR SHOE LACES 


Break force and extension at break of shoes laces can 
be tested in the dry state and in the wet state. A shoe 
lace is extended until it breaks using a tensile testing 
machine (see Fig. C.1). 


C-1 PROCEDURE 


Prepare three shoelace specimens of length sufficient 
to enable satisfactory clamping in the jaws while 
leaving a test length of 200 mm between them. After 


conditioning, extend each specimen by tensile testing 
with the machine whose jaws separate at a rate of 
100 mm/min until the test lace breaks. Record the 
maximum force obtained in Newton, and the extension 
at break if required. The arithmetic mean of three results 
is reported. If the test lace is constructed from several 
component parts, such as a case and a core, carefully 
watch the test specimen as it is extended and record the 
force when each of these component parts break.

Review of Indian Standards 


Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of 
‘BIS Catalogue’ and ‘Standards: Monthly Additions’.
